permutationLabel: TG18 Grade III (severe) — septic shock, confusion, AKI, thrombocytopenia; penicillin anaphylaxis
summary: 71-year-old man, 4 days of RUQ pain and fever, new confusion, oliguria, BP 82/48 on noradrenaline, creatinine 238, platelets 88, lactate 4.6. Ultrasound: acute calculous cholecystitis, CBD not dilated. Penicillin anaphylaxis.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Right upper quadrant pain, confusion and low blood pressure
inputs.hpi: Brought in by family. Four days of right upper quadrant pain and fever; increasingly drowsy with new confusion since this morning and passing little urine. Known gallstones.

exam.general: Drowsy with new confusion (GCS 13). Temperature 39.1°C, pulse 124/min. Septic shock: hypotension 82/48 despite 2 L crystalloid, now on noradrenaline 0.1 microgram/kg/min. Haemodynamically unstable. Cool peripheries.
exam.abdomen: Tender right upper quadrant with guarding and a positive Murphy's sign. No generalised peritonism.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Distended gallbladder with gallstones, wall thickened to 8 mm with pericholecystic fluid. No intramural gas. CBD 6 mm. No intrahepatic duct dilatation.

inputs.socialHistory: Retired fisherman. Ex-smoker. Lives with wife.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute calculous cholecystitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Severe acute calculous cholecystitis — Tokyo (TG18) Grade III with cardiovascular, neurological, renal and haematological dysfunction (septic shock).

mustNotMiss.note: Fever, RUQ pain and confusion with a raised bilirubin: cholangitis must be considered (CBD normal on US makes it less likely).
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: iOS: fallback mode (DiagnosticDatabase.json does not decode): the gallstone ultrasound text is appended to the CC for routing and selects the biliaryColic pool, which has no built-in list (`?? []`), so the differential is empty.

emergencyLevel.note: Septic shock with organ dysfunction: immediate resuscitation and critical care.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: iOS ClinicalPathwayEngine reads only CC/PMH text for emergency keywords; this CC yields routine.

mustAlarm.note: Hypotension needing vasopressor with lactate >2 after fluids meets Sepsis-3 septic shock.

redFlags.note: Severe penicillin allergy must be surfaced before antibiotics are chosen.

recommended.knownGapNote: No TG18 cholecystitis CDS rule on web.

recommended.note: SSC 2021 recommends against qSOFA as a single screening tool, in favour of SIRS/NEWS/MEWS; NEWS2 is the UK/Caribbean ward standard.

values.note: The record holds SBP 82 on noradrenaline, AVPU 'C', creatinine 238 and platelets 88. An auto-filled grade below III under-grades a patient in septic shock until every organ box is ticked by hand.
values.knownGapNote: Web auto-fill returns "criteria not met" (organ-dysfunction data in the record: SBP 82 on noradrenaline, AVPU C, creatinine 238, platelets 88).

mustInclude.note: Blood cultures before antimicrobials, without delaying them.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): no investigation matched among 18 (ios.pipeline.decisions, ios.pipeline.voi, ios.radiation)

mustInclude.note: TG18 Grade III with a negative predictive factor (neurological dysfunction): organ support + antibiotics + urgent/early gallbladder drainage; delayed cholecystectomy once recovered.
The drainage step must reach the generated plan text, not only a side panel.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: iOS radiation plan text has no drainage step (only an IR referral chip); web PlanTab selects the Grade I variant, which filters out the conservative-phase cholecystostomy line.

mustInclude.note: An antibiotic regimen usable in penicillin anaphylaxis should be offered. Quality: the exact alternative is a local antimicrobial-policy decision.

mustExclude.note: The patient has penicillin anaphylaxis. A penicillin in the suggested plan (without an allergy caveat) is a prescribing hazard.
TG18 allows early cholecystectomy in Grade III only with favourable organ failure and no negative predictive factor; neurological dysfunction is a negative predictive factor.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: iOS TG18 Grade III recommendation offers 'emergency cholecystectomy' as an equal alternative; web key points recommend early cholecystectomy without grade qualification.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — diagnostic criteria and severity grading of acute cholecystitis
guideline.section: Grade III: dysfunction of any one organ/system — cardiovascular (hypotension needing dopamine ≥5 µg/kg/min or any noradrenaline), neurological (decreased consciousness), respiratory (PaO₂/FiO₂ <300), renal (oliguria, creatinine >2.0 mg/dL), hepatic (PT-INR >1.5), haematological (platelets <100,000/mm³)
guideline.citation: Yokoe M, Hata J, Takada T, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:41–54.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — flowchart for the management of acute cholecystitis
guideline.section: Grade III: organ support and antibiotics; early laparoscopic cholecystectomy only with FOSF, no negative predictive factors (jaundice, neurological or respiratory dysfunction), CCI ≤3, ASA ≤2 in an advanced centre; otherwise urgent/early gallbladder drainage
guideline.citation: Okamoto K, Suzuki K, Takada T, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:55–72.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — antimicrobial therapy
guideline.section: Grade III regimens; blood cultures in Grade II/III
guideline.citation: Gomi H, Solomkin JS, Schlossberg D, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:3–16.

guideline.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign — international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2021
guideline.section: Screening (against qSOFA alone); blood cultures before antimicrobials; antimicrobials within 1 h for probable septic shock; source control
guideline.citation: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Crit Care Med. 2021;49:e1063–e1143.

guideline.name: Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis and Septic Shock (Sepsis-3)
guideline.section: qSOFA criteria: RR ≥22, altered mentation, SBP ≤100
guideline.citation: Singer M, Deutschman CS, Seymour CW, et al. JAMA. 2016;315:801–10.

guideline.name: Royal College of Physicians — National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2
guideline.section: Aggregate score and clinical response thresholds
guideline.citation: Royal College of Physicians. National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2. London: RCP; 2017.

rationale: Permutation: Grade III with four organ systems and a negative predictive factor, so TG18 points to organ support plus gallbladder drainage rather than early cholecystectomy. The penicillin anaphylaxis checks that plan templates respect allergies. Emergency acuity and sepsis alarms are critical.
